chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
He passed by a dump of rubbish full of filth and remarked: This is what the misers used to be niggardly about.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the nature of miserliness and worthless possessions?
ai.summary: In this concise aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) juxtaposes the physical reality of a dung heap with the spiritual state of the miser, illustrating that their hoarded wealth is ultimately as base and transient as excrement. This metaphor underscores the Shia ethical view that material accumulation without spiritual purpose reduces the miser to a state of degradation, where the object of their desire is unworthy of their devotion.
